audit.whatIsWrong: Chart read Skill/Cho'Gath/Cho'Gath/Skill/Skill/Cho'Gath/Cho'Gath while all seven whys say the opposite shape: whys[0] 'You out-tempo a slow, immobile Cho'Gath at level 1', whys[1] 'Your range and mobility keep you ahead through level 2', whys[2] 'your E-Q poke pressures him', whys[5] 'Your first-item crit Q re-establishes a trading edge', whys[6] 'a coin-flip on positioning'.
audit.why: Cho'Gath has no mobility at all; Rupture is a 6s telegraphed ground eruption at 950 range and Feral Scream needs 300 range. Yasuo dictates spacing until the Silence and Feast execute even it out at 4-6, then again on his first crit item, and the two-item game is genuinely a positioning coin-flip.
audit.corrected: Yasuo / Yasuo / Yasuo / Skill / Skill / Yasuo / Skill — identical to the packet chart and to all seven whys. Rows proposed as a matched full+content group.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why claimed 'E dashes through minions make you untouchable' at Level 2, where Yasuo has no E, and phases[6].why claimed his side-lane pattern is at full power on a row that is a coin-flip.
audit.why: The real Level 2 edge is tempo against an immobile champion on a 6s Rupture, not dash immunity. The real two-item read is that Feast is true damage and percent-health, so a resistance build does not answer it.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why now gives Rupture's 6s and the walk-up window; phases[6].why states the true-damage problem and the close-before-he-stacks instruction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places told the player to Wind Wall Rupture and Feral Scream: spikes[1] 'can Wind Wall (W) his Rupture and Scream', mid 'using Wind Wall on his Scream', wants.you[1] 'Wind Wall his Rupture windup and Scream'. spikes[3] also labelled Scream as his E.
audit.why: Rupture erupts from the ground at a target location and Feral Scream is a 300-range cone — neither is a projectile, so a wall does not touch either. Cho'Gath's kit has no projectile at all; the answers are side-stepping the Rupture telegraph and staying out of the cone. His E is Vorpal Spikes (the on-hit cone), not Scream.
audit.corrected: The Wind Wall claims replaced with side-stepping and cone spacing; the E slot credited to Vorpal Spikes. Added that Feast is true damage at 175 range so armour is the wrong answer.

edits.before: E dashes through minions make you untouchable in the wave. Only take the trade when Cho'Gath's Rupture is down.
edits.after: Cho'Gath is slow and Rupture is 6s on a 950 telegraph. Walk up between casts, take free autos, and give nothing back.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Cho'Gath carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in it is a coin-flip on positioning. Feast is true damage, so armour does not save you. Close before he stacks.

edits.before: Dashing INTO his engage with passive shield down — the wave is your armor; off it you are the squishiest melee alive.
edits.after: Feast is true damage at 175 range — armour never saves you; only staying above its execute threshold does.

edits.before: Cho'Gath's Feast (R) is a true-damage execute, so the danger flips once he hits 6 — but at even health you still control spacing and can Wind Wall (W) his Rupture and Scream, denying the setup he needs to land Feast.
edits.after: Cho'Gath's Feast (R) is a true-damage execute, so the danger flips once he hits 6 — but at even health you still control spacing and can side-step Rupture and his 300-range Scream cone, denying the setup he needs to land Feast.

edits.before: Cho'Gath scales into a monstrous frontline with Feast stacks and Vlad's-tier HP, so the longer the game the more his ult execute and Scream (E) DPS threaten you in teamfights — flank and avoid his cone.
edits.after: Cho'Gath scales into a monstrous frontline with Feast stacks and Vlad's-tier HP, so the longer the game the more his ult execute and Vorpal Spikes (E) DPS threaten you in teamfights — flank and avoid his cone.

edits.after: Through levels 3-6 you hold the tempo edge, dodging Rupture and staying out of his Scream cone, though the lane levels out once his Silence and, at 6, his Feast execute give him a hard punish for over-committing.
